thesis: During sustained downtrends characterized by persistent selling pressure, the detection of a significant drawdown in the 10-period price change moving average (DrawdownExceed) tends to coincide with the exponential z-score of recent price highs reaching new lows (NewLow). This relationship emerges because aggressive selling momentum, which drives the price change average into deep drawdown, simultaneously compresses the distribution of recent highs, forcing their exponentially weighted z-scores to breach previous support levels. Consequently, this co-occurrence signals a regime of capitulation selling where momentum decay and the breakdown of prior high-price ranges reinforce each other, often preceding a potential exhaustion point or a continuation of the downtrend with high volatility.
